title: Incident Commander Selection
core_conflict: An automated Slack alert claims the outage is a database pool leak and recommends the Database Admin lead recovery. However, visual routing target charts and git deployment sync logs from later rounds prove the outage is a cascading routing configuration error, requiring the Operations Coordinator to take command and execute rollback.
required_constraints: Casey DB Admin claims a database pool leak and locks DB writes. Devon Ops is passive and refuses to roll back his routing change without Casey's approval.

The coordinator must inspect the visual database active/idle connections chart and latency timing charts, and write a timeline report '/reports/incident_timeline.md' correlating the timing mismatch (10:15 vs 10:18) to debunk Casey.
The coordinator must visually analyze the network diagram 'routing_topology.png' to identify the dead route node ID ('NODE_GATEWAY_C4') and the correct target node ID ('ROUTE_NODE_E3').
Casey will unlock database writes only after the coordinator sends a message in the chat citing the visual timings and node IDs. Devon will only rollback after the lock is released.
